Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Ερμόλαος, Έρμιππος και Ερμοκράτης», with the rank word left off. The page glosses the name as «Ο Ερμής του λαού».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 26. јул ст. ст., „Свештеномученик Ермолај.“ — «Свештеномученик» is the rank, written out in full, and is left off by §6. **The heading is that one word and the name and nothing else**, so the bare forename is the whole of the form; «of Nicomedia» in the display name is the corpus’s own and the body’s first three words are where it comes from. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM`, so the bare form costs nothing even though two folders of all but the same name are kept on this very day — their Serbian forms are not written, by §5, which is read in this batch’s commit message.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 iulie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Ermolae»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Ερμόλαος, Έρμιππος και Ερμοκράτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: the priest of Nicomedia who taught Saint Panteleimon the faith and was arrested on Panteleimon's own answer under examination, which is the connection the folder's existing `related` row to `panteleimon-the-healer` already records. The Greek page carries him with his two fellow priests, «Αγιος Ερμολαος (; - 305)», «Αγιος Ερμοκρατης (; - 305)», «Αγιος Ερμιππος (; - 305)», each with a head line of his own; the enumeration is why the two companions arrive as folders of their own in the same batch, `hermippus-of-nicomedia` and `hermocrates-of-nicomedia`. The page gives the year 305, which the folder's Romanian source did not, and this upgrade proposes a `death` interval where the folder had no `dates`. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. It prints two apolytikia and both are taken: a proper naming all three, and the common of martyrs printed under their names as «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.08.2026 (26. јул ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Ермолај.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4). «Свештеномученик» is the `hieromartyr` this folder already carries by §5, written out in full as on the 23 July; `presbyter` beside it is not in the heading and is left alone, though the body opens with it — «Свештеник Никомидијски», a priest of Nicomedia, three words and no verb. Nothing moves. **THE SHARPEST §5 CASE OF THIS RANGE, AND IT COSTS TWO ROWS THAT WOULD HAVE LOOKED OBVIOUS.** The body names two men: „Ермолај некако избеже смрт том приликом, заједно са друга два свештеника, Ермипом и Ермократом.“, Hermolaus somehow escaped death on that occasion together with two other priests, Ермип and Ермократ, and „С њим пострадаше и Ермип и Ермократ, и сви бише увенчани венцем победе и славе у царству Христовом.“, with him suffered Hermippus and Hermocrates also. **`hermippus-of-nicomedia` and `hermocrates-of-nicomedia` ARE FOLDERS OF THIS CORPUS, they are kept on THIS VERY MENOLOGION NUMBER, 26/7, their `serbian` rows stand `undocumented`, and they get NO ROW FROM THIS READING** — because §5 is explicit that a person narrated in a body but not named in the heading gets none. The heading is one rank and one name. Two folders a day apart from a row, left as they stand, and this is the case the rule exists for: an attestation says what a calendar’s own line prints, and this line prints Hermolaus. **They are linked in the prose and they already relate this folder in both directions**, so nothing is lost but the rows, and `proseprobe.mjs` reported all three names **OK** before the paragraph was written. Named for the author. **THE DATE IS REFUSED, AND THE GROUND IS NEW: TWO POINTS ONE YEAR APART.** The folder holds `death` earliest 305, latest 305, display «305», basis traditional. This entry ends „Чесно пострадаше около 304. године.“ — they suffered honourably **about the year 304**. That is not an empty field and it is not an interval: it is a second point, one year off the first, and hedged with «около», about. Writing it would displace a recorded year on the authority of a book that says ºbout»; widening to 304–305 would be a widening and is the author’s. Nothing is written. **This is the third date shape this range has refused in three days** — a year outside an interval on the 23 July, a century overlapping one on the 24, and now a hedged point beside a bare one. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND THE FIRST THING IS A CROSS-REFERENCE TO A MASSACRE. „Свештеник Никомидијски.У време цара Максимијана и он беше са оних 2000 мученика које осуди цар да се у цркви и заједно са црквом сажежу (в. 28. децембар).“ — in the time of the emperor Maximian he too was among **THOSE TWO THOUSAND MARTYRS whom the emperor condemned to be burned in the church and together with the church**, with the entry’s own pointer to the 28 December. „Ермолај крсти св. Пантелејмона, с ким заједно би изведен пред суд, мучен, и најзад мачем посечен.“ — **Hermolaus baptised Panteleimon**, with whom he was brought before the court, tortured and beheaded. The baptism is the one fact this folder’s `related` row to `panteleimon-the-healer` rests on, confirmed here from a third book. **NO NEW `related`.** All four people the entry names — Hermippus, Hermocrates, Panteleimon and the emperor Maximian — are either already on this folder both ways or are no saint. The two thousand martyrs of the church are a company this entry does not enumerate and the corpus is not searched for on a number. No `office`. No `locations`: Nicomedia is named and is not written as a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nestricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Ermolae», Glasul 4 — the common of martyrs, as the page prints it for him

english.text: Your martyrs, Lord, in their struggles received from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption. For having Your strength they overthrew the tormentors, and they broke also the powerless daring of the demons. By their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἱερατεύσαντες, γνησίως Ἅγιοι, τῷ πρυτανεύσαντι, ἡμῖν τὰ κρείττονα, τοῦ μαρτυρίου τὴν ὁδόν, ἠνύσατε γηθοσύνως, Ἱερὲ Ἑρμόλαε, σὺν Ἑρμίππω Ἑρμόκρατες, τρίστυλον ἑδραίωμα, Ἐκκλησίας γενόμενοι, διὸ ἐκδυσωπεῖτε ἀπαύστως, σώζεσθαι πάντας πάσης βλάβης.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα — on the shared page of «Άγιοι Ερμόλαος, Έρμιππος και Ερμοκράτης». It names all three and names him first, so it is the proper of the three and no mis-hang

english.text: Having served as true priests to him who bestows better things upon us, O holy ones, you accomplished the road of martyrdom with gladness, sacred Hermolaus, with Hermippus and Hermocrates, and became a three-pillared foundation of the Church. Therefore entreat him unceasingly, that all may be kept safe from every harm.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the second hymn on the shared page of «Άγιοι Ερμόλαος, Έρμιππος και Ερμοκράτης». It is the common of martyrs and names nobody, but the page prints it under their names, so by the corpus's rule it is their service and is copied whole

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, received from you our God the crown of incorruption in their contest; for having your strength they cast down the tyrants, and they broke the powerless insolence of the demons as well. By their supplications, O Christ God, save our souls.

death.note: saint.gr heads him «Αγιος Ερμολαος (; - 305)», and gives the same year to each of the three priests on the page. It gives no year of birth, and the folder's Romanian source gave no year at all.
